{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"Mara stopped.

The whisper came again, this time from the kitchen doorway. Her mother stood there, one hand resting on the frame. “You can come home,” she said.

Mira seized Mara’s sleeve. “That isn’t her.”

The woman’s expression softened. “I know the song you sang when the storms frightened you.”

Mara remembered the tune, but not the words. She remembered a warm hand smoothing her hair, and the smell of rain in the garden. The river’s edge pressed against her shoes.

Tomas held out the paper boat. Its little folded sail had begun to glow.

“Read the ink,” Mara said.

He turned it over. The words had changed: NOT EVERY DOOR LEADS OUT.

The kitchen flickered. For an instant, Mara saw what lay beyond it: not a summer house, but a long corridor lined with clocks. At its far end, a girl in a red coat ran toward them, carrying a lantern.

Mira’s breath caught. “That’s my brother.”

One of the circling names flared overhead. It was Tomas’s, bright as a struck match. The river tugged at his waist, drawing him backward.

Mara thrust the boat into his hands. “Follow the lantern.”

He stared at her. “What about you?”

She looked from the false doorway to the dark water. Her mother’s face waited in the kitchen, patient and impossible.

“I’ll find the real way.”

The watch gave a sharp click. Its second hand spun backward, and the river fell away from Tomas like a curtain.

Mira grabbed his hand. Together they ran toward the lantern.

Mara stayed behind as the kitchen door vanished."}
